target_customer: Companies onboarding employees to their own data with BI, SQL, R and Python training
problem: Employees lacked skills to answer business questions with data. Leada offered online data science and analytics training, pivoting from academic learners to enterprise.
business_model: B2B training subscription sold to enterprises

founders.name: Brian Liou
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as sole founder with no bio.

competitors.name: DataCamp
competitors.what: Online data science courses that added a group feature for university classes and enterprise teams
competitors.traction_then: About 300,000 learners had taken its courses
competitors.funding_then: New 1 million dollar funding announced with the group feature

competitors.name: Coursera, edX and Udacity
competitors.what: Online course platforms named as other places to build data science skills

technical_complexity.rationale: Course content and a hosted learning environment; the effort was content creation more than engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Course content was copyable and large platforms like Coursera and DataCamp offered similar training.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: DataCamp added enterprise team features by February 2016. No source found on any acquisition of Leada.

market_need_then: Data science skills were in demand in 2015, shown by platforms like DataCamp reaching about 300,000 learners per a February 2016 article, but no Leada traction or revenue figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Used teamleada.com rather than leada.com per the YC page

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found, only the pivot story. The name resembles words like lead and leader.

pivots.from: Data science training for academics and students
pivots.to: Enterprise data science training for employees
pivots.why: Academic focus did not gain traction per VentureBeat

outcome_analysis: Leada was a one person YC S15 company selling data science training that pivoted from academics to enterprise because the academic focus did not gain traction. It raised roughly 120 thousand to 200 thousand dollars and is listed as inactive or dead, with no shutdown post-mortem found, so the cause is not public. Larger platforms such as DataCamp and Coursera served the same need.
notes: teamleada.com failed DNS resolution, so the site is treated as dead or unreachable. The VentureBeat article was not opened because the fetch safety check was rate limited; its claims come from search summaries (pivot, 200K total from YC and Imagine K12, 2016 date). Funding totals conflict: VentureBeat says 200K, CB Insights 140K, Bouncewatch a 120K YC seed on 2015-08-18 (single aggregator). The Imagine K12 round has no stated amount or date. Competitor sources are dated February 2016, about six months after the batch, which is outside a few months; they are kept with this caveat because no earlier dated source was found. Founder education and prior employers were not found.
